written:
## 1. The numbers
Risk-off. Tech and AI names led the slide, and the jump in the VIX shows investors are paying up for protection ahead of tonight's Nvidia report.

## 2. What moved and why
**AI sell-off deepens before Nvidia reports**
Why it happened: US stocks fell faster ahead of Nvidia's first earnings release without Jensen Huang running the company. Chip stocks have also been under pressure from US export curbs.
Why it matters: Nvidia is the biggest weight in the market, so its results and guidance will set the tone for the whole AI trade.

**Treasury yields stay above 5% as markets price Fed hikes**
Why it happened: Retail sales met expectations, but the core measure excluding gas and autos beat forecasts. Oil gains and expectations of further Fed hikes had already pushed the 10-year above 5% last week.
Why it matters: Higher yields cut the present value of long-dated tech earnings and keep borrowing costs high for companies and homebuyers.

**Canadian yields fall as rate-hike bets ease**
Why it happened: Canadian inflation data offered some relief, potentially easing pressure on the Bank of Canada to tighten further. Energy and other resource stocks also fell Monday.
Why it matters: Canadian and US bond markets are moving in opposite directions, so the Bank of Canada looks less hawkish than the Fed.

## Deals
- **Acquisition: Canadian Natural Resources → Advantage Energy** (about C$2.53 billion including debt). The deal adds Montney and Charlie Lake production next to assets Canadian Natural already owns.
- **Acquisition: Diamondback → Double Eagle drilling portfolio (reported, not confirmed)** (about $5 billion, according to the FT). Diamondback is reportedly close to buying a Permian drilling portfolio.

## Already out today
- 8:30 AM: US October retail sales. Up 0.2% vs 0.2% expected. Spending is holding up despite high rates.
- 8:30 AM: Retail sales control group. Up 0.6% vs 0.4% expected. The stronger core reading gives the Fed less reason to ease off.
- Pre-market: Home Depot Q3. EPS of $3.86; revenue of $43.4B; comparable sales up 2.2% vs EPS $3.84 expected. The stock still dipped about 2% after management announced a CEO handover.
- Pre-market: Disney Q4. EPS of $1.77. The beat helped limit the market's losses.

## 3. What's coming today
- Later today: Fed officials' remarks. They may signal how firmly a December hike is being considered.
- About 4:20 PM: Nvidia fiscal Q3 results. The report is expected at about 4:20 p.m. ET. It is the first one under interim CEO Kress.
- Wed: Lowe's and TJX earnings. Both report Wednesday. They give more evidence on consumer spending.
- This week: Anthropic IPO. It is set to test investor appetite for AI.

## 4. Canada corner
- TSX: The index closed Monday at 35,722.13 after a 1.1% drop. Banks, energy and materials were the main drags.
- Bank of Canada: It raised rates in October. Softer inflation has reduced hike bets for December, though the Fed looks more hawkish.
- Loonie: The Canadian dollar closed Monday at 69.93 US cents. It is steady against a firm US dollar.
- Notable company: Canadian Natural's Advantage deal is Canada's biggest energy deal of the week so far.

## 5. The takeaway
If someone asks you about markets today: AI-led equity weakness and Treasury yields above 5% are feeding each other. Nvidia's guidance and the Fed's December hike odds are the two swing factors.
Consulting angle: Nvidia's governance shake-up shows how dependent a company's strategy can be on one founder. Boards at similar firms should have succession plans and compliance oversight in place before a crisis forces them.
Accounting angle: Canadian Natural's Advantage purchase would be a business combination. Assets and liabilities would be measured at fair value, the premium over book value would go to goodwill or to oil and gas properties, and auditors would focus on the reserve-based valuations.

stories.title: AI sell-off deepens before Nvidia reports
stories.why_happened: US stocks fell faster ahead of Nvidia's first earnings release without Jensen Huang running the company. Chip stocks have also been under pressure from US export curbs.
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is the biggest weight in the market, so its results and guidance will set the tone for the whole AI trade.
stories.full: AI stocks dragged the US market lower on Monday, led by Nvidia, and the S&P 500 notched a third straight loss. Nvidia fell 4.1% on Monday. Tonight is the first time interim CEO Colette Kress will speak to Wall Street since taking over from Huang. Nvidia is setting up a new board committee for national security and global trade compliance, after revelations about Huang's personal conduct. The stock pared early losses after Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO if the board decided that was best for shareholders. Earnings and revenue are expected to be up about 90% from a year ago. A beat and raise is widely expected, but the bigger question is earnings visibility beyond 2028. Chip designers and AI infrastructure names lose most if guidance disappoints. Broadcom and CoreWeave held up better this morning. Watch the CEO-succession answer on tonight's call and any comment on China export rules.

stories.title: Treasury yields stay above 5% as markets price Fed hikes
stories.why_happened: Retail sales met expectations, but the core measure excluding gas and autos beat forecasts. Oil gains and expectations of further Fed hikes had already pushed the 10-year above 5% last week.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields cut the present value of long-dated tech earnings and keep borrowing costs high for companies and homebuyers.
stories.full: Rates are driving the equity wobble as much as AI is. Hot inflation data and comments from a Fed official pushed traders to bet on more aggressive hikes. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, a bit below forecasts, but the annual rate of 6.5% was the highest since November 2022. A 10-year Treasury auction also drew soft demand. One prediction market put the odds of a 25-basis-point December hike at 89%. The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed expectations most closely, was around 4.85% this morning. Higher yields hit long-duration growth stocks hardest. They also keep fixed mortgage rates elevated. Watch remarks from Fed officials later today. Chair Warsh's comments on the 17th are a focus.

stories.title: Canadian yields fall as rate-hike bets ease
stories.why_happened: Canadian inflation data offered some relief, potentially easing pressure on the Bank of Canada to tighten further. Energy and other resource stocks also fell Monday.
stories.why_matters: Canadian and US bond markets are moving in opposite directions, so the Bank of Canada looks less hawkish than the Fed.
stories.full: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate in October, and investors are watching whether persistent prices could force more tightening. Before the latest CPI, money markets priced about a 60% chance of a December hike. The TSX fell 1.1% on Monday to 35,722.13. On the TSX Venture Exchange, materials fell 3.6% and energy lost 2.4%, with gold stocks down 2.8%. The TSX is heavy in banks, energy and materials, so it is exposed to commodity swings and to rate expectations. Watch whether softer Canadian price pressures hold up in later data. A wider gap between US and Canadian rates also tends to keep the loonie under pressure.

deals.why: The deal adds Montney and Charlie Lake production next to assets Canadian Natural already owns.
deals.full: Canadian Natural will pay C$13.55 per share, an equity value of about C$2.255 billion. That is 25% above Advantage's Friday close. It will be done through a plan of arrangement and is expected to close in Q1 2027. It will be funded from cash on hand and existing bank credit facilities. The deal brings about 79,000 boe/d of production. Management points to scale synergies and better area efficiency. Canadian Natural says it will keep its free cash flow allocation policy. Canadian Natural's shares fell about 2.5% in Toronto. It is one of several recent Canadian oil and gas tie-ups.

deals.target: Double Eagle drilling portfolio (reported, not confirmed)
deals.value: about $5 billion, according to the FT
deals.why: Diamondback is reportedly close to buying a Permian drilling portfolio.
deals.full: Only the FT's reported size and parties are available so far, and no terms have been confirmed. Deals like this and Canadian Natural's purchase create public price benchmarks for producing wells and undeveloped drilling locations. The pattern across both deals is producers consolidating their best basins, which signals confidence in oil-linked cash flows even as oil trades near $90.

intern.headline: AI stocks slide before Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings
intern.mood: Risk-off (investors are nervous and want safer places for their money). Tech and AI stocks led the slide. The jump in the VIX (a gauge of how scared investors are) shows people are paying more to protect themselves ahead of tonight's Nvidia report.

stories.title: AI sell-off deepens before Nvidia reports
stories.why_happened: US stocks fell faster ahead of Nvidia's first earnings report without Jensen Huang running the company. Chip stocks have also been under pressure from US export curbs (government rules that limit which countries can buy certain chips).
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is the biggest weight in the market (it makes up a large share of the index). Its results and guidance (what the company expects to happen next) will set the mood for the whole AI trade.
stories.full: AI stocks dragged the US market lower on Monday, led by Nvidia. The S&P 500 (a basket of 500 large US companies, used as a market scoreboard) had a third straight loss. Nvidia fell 4.1% on Monday. Tonight is the first time interim CEO (temporary boss) Colette Kress will speak to Wall Street since taking over from Huang. Nvidia is setting up a new board committee (a small group of directors who check specific issues) for national security and global trade compliance. This comes after revelations about Huang's personal conduct. The stock pared early losses after Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO if the board decided that was best for shareholders (the company's owners). Earnings and revenue are expected to be up about 90% from a year ago. A beat and raise (results better than expected, and a higher outlook) is widely expected. The bigger question is earnings visibility beyond 2028, meaning how clearly the company can see its profits further into the future. Chip designers and AI infrastructure companies lose the most if guidance disappoints. Broadcom and CoreWeave held up better this morning. Watch the CEO-succession answer on tonight's call and any comment on China export rules.

stories.title: Treasury yields stay above 5% as markets price Fed hikes
stories.why_happened: Retail sales met expectations, but the core measure (which leaves out gas and car sales) beat forecasts. Oil gains and expectations of further Fed hikes had already pushed the 10-year above 5% last week.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields (the interest rate on bonds) cut the present value of long-dated tech earnings (today's worth of profits expected far in the future). They also keep borrowing costs high for companies and homebuyers.
stories.full: Rates are driving the market wobble as much as AI is. Hot inflation data (prices rising quickly) and comments from a Fed official pushed traders to bet on more aggressive hikes. The Fed is the US central bank, and a rate hike means it raises the interest rate to slow prices. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, a bit below forecasts. But the annual rate of 6.5% was the highest since November 2022. A 10-year Treasury auction (a sale of 10-year US government bonds) also drew soft demand, meaning fewer buyers than hoped. One prediction market put the odds of a 25-basis-point December hike at 89%. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so 25 basis points is a quarter of a percentage point. The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed expectations most closely, was around 4.85% this morning. Higher yields hit long-duration growth stocks hardest, because their big profits are far away. They also keep fixed mortgage rates high. Watch remarks from Fed officials later today. Chair Warsh's comments on the 17th are a focus.

stories.title: Canadian yields fall as rate-hike bets ease
stories.why_happened: Canadian inflation data offered some relief. This may ease pressure on the Bank of Canada (Canada's central bank) to raise rates further. Energy and other resource stocks also fell Monday.
stories.why_matters: Canadian and US bond markets are moving in opposite directions, so the Bank of Canada looks less tough on inflation than the Fed.
stories.full: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate in October. Investors are watching whether prices that keep rising could force more rate hikes. Before the latest CPI (consumer price index, a main measure of inflation), money markets priced about a 60% chance of a December hike. The TSX (the main Canadian stock index) fell 1.1% on Monday to 35,722.13. On the TSX Venture Exchange (a market for smaller companies), materials fell 3.6% and energy lost 2.4%. Gold stocks fell 2.8%. The TSX has many banks, energy companies and mining companies, so it moves a lot when commodity prices (oil, metals and similar goods) swing and when interest rate expectations change. Watch whether softer Canadian price pressures hold up in later data. A wider gap between US and Canadian rates also tends to keep the loonie (Canada's dollar) under pressure.

deals.value: About C$2.53 billion including debt (money the company owes)
deals.why: The deal adds Montney and Charlie Lake production (oil and gas output from two areas in Western Canada) next to assets Canadian Natural already owns.
deals.full: Canadian Natural will pay C$13.55 per share. That gives an equity value (the value of the shares) of about C$2.255 billion. The price is 25% above Advantage's Friday close, meaning what its shares last traded for at the end of the week. The deal will be done through a plan of arrangement (a legal process used to restructure a company). It is expected to close in Q1 2027, the first quarter of 2027. It will be funded from cash on hand and existing bank credit facilities (pre-approved loans from banks). The deal brings about 79,000 boe/d of production. Boe/d means barrels of oil equivalent per day, a way to measure oil and gas output. Management points to scale synergies (savings from being bigger) and better area efficiency. Canadian Natural says it will keep its free cash flow allocation policy, meaning how it plans to use the cash the business generates. Canadian Natural's shares fell about 2.5% in Toronto. It is one of several recent Canadian oil and gas tie-ups.

deals.target: Double Eagle drilling portfolio (reported, not confirmed)
deals.value: About $5 billion, according to the FT (Financial Times)
deals.why: Diamondback is reportedly close to buying a Permian drilling portfolio (a group of oil drilling assets in the Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico).
deals.full: Only the FT's reported size and parties are available so far. No terms have been confirmed. Deals like this and Canadian Natural's purchase create public price benchmarks (reference prices) for producing wells and undeveloped drilling locations. The pattern across both deals is producers consolidating their best basins (big oil and gas regions). This signals confidence in oil-linked cash flows, even as oil trades near $90 a barrel.

intern.takeaway: If someone asks you about markets today: falling AI stocks and Treasury yields above 5% are pushing on each other. Nvidia's results and the odds of a December Fed rate hike are the two things that could move markets most.
intern.takeaway_consulting: Nvidia's leadership change shows how much a company's strategy can depend on one founder. Firms like it should have succession plans (plans for who leads next) and compliance oversight (checks that rules are followed) in place before a crisis forces them.
intern.takeaway_accounting: Canadian Natural's purchase of Advantage would count as a business combination. The buyer records the assets and liabilities at fair value (their current market value). The extra price paid above book value (the value on the company's books) would go to goodwill (an intangible asset) or to oil and gas properties. Auditors would focus on the reserve-based valuations (estimates of how much oil and gas is recoverable).

partner.headline: AI stocks slide before Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings
partner.mood: Risk-off. Tech and AI names led the slide, and the jump in the VIX shows investors are paying up for protection ahead of tonight's Nvidia report.

stories.title: AI sell-off deepens before Nvidia reports
stories.why_happened: US stocks fell faster ahead of Nvidia's first earnings release without Jensen Huang running the company. Chip stocks have also been under pressure from US export curbs.
stories.why_matters: Nvidia is the largest index weight, so its results and guidance will set the tone for the whole AI trade. Second-order: a guidance miss would compress forward multiples across semis and AI infrastructure, and a beat-and-raise would likely be sold unless visibility extends beyond 2028, since the market is pricing duration risk rather than the next quarter.
stories.full: AI stocks dragged the US market lower on Monday, led by Nvidia, and the S&P 500 notched a third straight loss. Nvidia fell 4.1% on Monday. Tonight is the first time interim CEO Colette Kress will speak to Wall Street since taking over from Huang. Nvidia is setting up a new board committee for national security and global trade compliance, after revelations about Huang's personal conduct. The stock pared early losses after Huang said he would be willing to return as CEO if the board decided that was best for shareholders. Earnings and revenue are expected to be up about 90% from a year ago. A beat and raise is widely expected, but the bigger question is earnings visibility beyond 2028. Chip designers and AI infrastructure names lose most if guidance disappoints. Broadcom and CoreWeave held up better this morning. Watch the CEO-succession answer on tonight's call and any comment on China export rules.

stories.title: Treasury yields stay above 5% as markets price Fed hikes
stories.why_happened: Retail sales met expectations, but the core measure excluding gas and autos beat forecasts. Oil gains and expectations of further Fed hikes had already pushed the 10-year above 5% last week.
stories.why_matters: Higher yields compress the present value of long-duration tech earnings and keep borrowing costs high for companies and homebuyers. Second-order: with the 2-year near 4.85% and a December hike priced at 89%, the front end is tracking policy directly, so the curve dynamics and any hawkish Fed signal would flow into IG and HY spreads and into the rate-sensitive multiples of growth equities.
stories.full: Rates are driving the equity wobble as much as AI is. Hot inflation data and comments from a Fed official pushed traders to bet on more aggressive hikes. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, a bit below forecasts, but the annual rate of 6.5% was the highest since November 2022. A 10-year Treasury auction also drew soft demand. One prediction market put the odds of a 25-basis-point December hike at 89%. The 2-year yield, which tracks Fed expectations most closely, was around 4.85% this morning. Higher yields hit long-duration growth stocks hardest. They also keep fixed mortgage rates elevated. Watch remarks from Fed officials later today. Chair Warsh's comments on the 17th are a focus.

stories.title: Canadian yields fall as rate-hike bets ease
stories.why_happened: Canadian inflation data offered some relief, potentially easing pressure on the Bank of Canada to tighten further. Energy and other resource stocks also fell Monday.
stories.why_matters: Canadian and US bond markets are moving in opposite directions, so the Bank of Canada looks less hawkish than the Fed. Second-order: the widening US-Canada rate differential points to continued loonie pressure, and the TSX's heavy weighting in banks, energy and materials means the index is more sensitive to commodity and rate-path repricing than to the US AI trade.
stories.full: The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate in October, and investors are watching whether persistent prices could force more tightening. Before the latest CPI, money markets priced about a 60% chance of a December hike. The TSX fell 1.1% on Monday to 35,722.13. On the TSX Venture Exchange, materials fell 3.6% and energy lost 2.4%, with gold stocks down 2.8%. The TSX is heavy in banks, energy and materials, so it is exposed to commodity swings and to rate expectations. Watch whether softer Canadian price pressures hold up in later data. A wider gap between US and Canadian rates also tends to keep the loonie under pressure.

deals.why: The deal adds Montney and Charlie Lake production next to assets Canadian Natural already owns. Second-order: it sets a public benchmark for Montney producing assets and supports consolidation multiples for Canadian gas-weighted peers.
deals.full: Canadian Natural will pay C$13.55 per share, an equity value of about C$2.255 billion. That is 25% above Advantage's Friday close. It will be done through a plan of arrangement and is expected to close in Q1 2027. It will be funded from cash on hand and existing bank credit facilities. The deal brings about 79,000 boe/d of production. Management points to scale synergies and better area efficiency. Canadian Natural says it will keep its free cash flow allocation policy. Canadian Natural's shares fell about 2.5% in Toronto. It is one of several recent Canadian oil and gas tie-ups. Funding from cash and existing bank facilities, rather than new debt or equity, means leverage metrics are not expected to change materially at close. The 25% premium and the share price reaction suggest the market is weighing the premium against the acquirer's balance sheet.

deals.target: Double Eagle drilling portfolio (reported, not confirmed)
deals.value: About $5 billion, according to the FT
deals.why: Diamondback is reportedly close to buying a Permian drilling portfolio. Second-order: if confirmed, it would set a benchmark for Permian undeveloped locations and inventory pricing, which feeds into acquirer valuations on a per-location basis.
deals.full: Only the FT's reported size and parties are available so far, and no terms have been confirmed. Deals like this and Canadian Natural's purchase create public price benchmarks for producing wells and undeveloped drilling locations. The pattern across both deals is producers consolidating their best basins, which signals confidence in oil-linked cash flows even as oil trades near $90.
